findings.finding: KEYS goes into the print de-rated: -26.4% from its $389.93 high of 2026-10-06, -8.3% over 20 days and -6.1% over 5 days (baseline), 23% below the October high by 2026-11-02 against S&P -3.5%, and ~33% below a $425 mean target; Trefis attributes the Jul 31-Nov 8 fall to a -28.7% P/E change while revenue grew 36%. The real bar is therefore lower than the whisper suggests.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: After a sell-off into Q4 FY25 and Q1 FY26 the beats were bought +10.0% and +23.1%; after a run-up into Q2/Q3 FY26 the beats were sold -0.6% and -6.3% (baseline).
findings.why_not_priced: The de-rating is itself the price; the finding is that the bar a beat must clear is lower than three months ago. If the market were pricing a clean beat and guide, the stock would not be at its lows into the print with downside skew bid.
findings.independence: Baseline run-up fields (sealed); Fintel mean target $424.98 vs $286.78 on 2026-11-04 (https://fintel.io/s/gb/0a7n); Earnings Whispers bullish sentiment 28.3% from 35.8% (https://finviz.com/news/421346/keysights-supply-chain-not-demand-sets-the-bar-for-a-record-fourth-quarter).

findings.finding: The Earnings Whisper is $3.49, above the $3.34-3.40 guide and the $3.36 consensus, and Keysight beat the high end of its guide in Q3 (EPS $3.07 vs ~$2.48 consensus); with Q4 revenue guided only ~5% above Q3 because supply governs, an in-guide or slightly-above print may read as a pause against a whisper bar above consensus.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Q3 FY26 EPS beat of ~24% sold -6.3%; Q2 FY26 beat -0.6% (baseline); the reported quarter has not paid on the last two prints.
findings.why_not_priced: The whisper is public, so this is the market's own bar; the finding is that the gap between guide and whisper is narrow room under a supply cap. If the market expected a large beat, the stock would not have fallen 6% in the five days before the print.
findings.independence: Zacks consensus $3.36 and ~$1.94bn (https://www.zacks.com/stock/news/3030409/can-strong-revenue-growth-boost-keysights-q4-earnings); Zacks ESP does not predict a beat. Shares the Earnings Whispers preview with finding 1.

findings.finding: On 2026-11-02, in the CFO-succession release (Jason Kary, EISG president, replaces 13-year CFO Neil Dougherty on 2026-12-18; Dougherty stays as adviser through FY27, 'planned succession'), Keysight said 'Demand across Keysight's end markets remains strong' and that it is not updating its Q4 outlook: an implicit reaffirmation two days after quarter-end, with no pre-announced upside.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No prior CFO change at Keysight in the record; the stock closed 23% below its October high on Nov 2, the release day, and kept falling to ~$273 by Nov 9 per Trefis data.
findings.why_not_priced: The release says the quarter closed Oct 31 with demand strong and no change to the guide, which rules out a miss on demand; the market sold the stock through it anyway, so the 'no miss' content is not reflected in a price that fell further after it. The departing CFO giving his last guide is a small risk of a conservative Q1 frame.
findings.independence: Sept 11 Goldman remarks also reiterated the $1.94bn Q4 midpoint (https://quartr.com/events/keysight-technologies-inc-keys-goldman-sachs-communacopia-technology-conference-2026_3gx1pBHu).

findings.finding: At Goldman Sachs Communacopia (2026-09-11) management said about $100M of orders had slipped beyond the normal shipment window on component bottlenecks, reiterated Q4 at $1.94bn, and said revenue should exceed $2bn a quarter once constraints ease; with orders above $2bn for three straight quarters and book-to-bill above 1.1, a Q1 FY27 guide at or above $2bn is possible if supply loosens, against street ~$1.95-1.96bn.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Guide above street bought +10.0% (Nov 2025) and +23.1% (Feb 2026); a guide above street with a supply warning sold -6.3% (Aug 2026) (baseline; https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/22/why-keysight-technologies-stock-sank-this-week/).
findings.why_not_priced: The stock fell 5.2% on 2026-09-14 on this supply talk (https://www.quiverquant.com/news/Keysight+Technologies+Slides+as+AI+Hardware+Weakness+and+Supply-Constraint+Talk+Weigh+on+Shares), so the market read the slip as a negative while the same remark sizes deferred revenue that lands in later quarters; a Q1 guide of ~$1.95bn street does not reflect a backlog release. Sized small because the CFO said on Aug 18 the constraint would limit conversion for about two quarters, i.e. through Q1.
findings.independence: CFO on 2026-08-18: 'demand is not the limiter', supply 'likely to be nonlinear' for about two quarters (https://www.tradingkey.com/news/transcripts/262116238-tradingkey); Ralliant flagged 'constrained supply' on 2026-11-04, so the component squeeze persisted into the quarter.

findings.finding: The CFO said on the Q3 call that one-time tariff impacts 'artificially pulled up '26 profitability that won't repeat', so the FY27 frame and the Q1 EPS guide start from a base that includes a non-recurring benefit; the leverage target (>40% incrementals) is stated ex one-time items, which leaves room for a Q1 EPS guide below what a naive extrapolation of Q4's ~$3.37 implies.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The Aug 2026 print sold -6.3% / -11.7% on the week when management flagged softer FY27 growth/margin risk (https://www.fool.com/investing/2026/08/22/why-keysight-technologies-stock-sank-this-week/).
findings.why_not_priced: It is public but the FY27 EPS consensus is stale and scattered ($8.77 to ~$10.97 across pages), so it is unclear the street netted the tariff item out; if it had, the Q1 EPS consensus would sit visibly below Q4's level. Sized small because management also says gross margin in the upper 60s is sustainable and synergies add ~$50M into FY27.
findings.independence: Earnings Whispers preview (2026-11-11) names the non-recurring tariff benefit as a key test; Ralliant and Viavi both carried IEEPA tariff refunds in their September quarters (https://finviz.com/news/415674/ralliant-beats-and-raises-again-as-growth-accelerates-to-17-but-tariff-refunds-and-inventory-build-temper-the-margin-story).

findings.finding: Reaction history: the last two Keysight prints were beats that sold (-0.59% May 2026, -6.32% Aug 2026, the latter on a ~24% EPS beat, a revenue beat above the guide high end and a raised outlook), so this name's market currently pays for the forward frame, not the quarter.
findings.why_not_priced: History, not news; it caps the payoff of the quarter line. The two up moves came when the stock went in de-rated (as now), which is why this is sized small and finding 1 carries the offset.
findings.independence: Peer Ralliant (Tektronix) beat and raised on 2026-11-04 and later traded -12.2% (finviz page quote), the same beat-sold pattern in test and measurement this season.

findings.finding: Viavi (reported 2026-11-04, quarter to Oct 3) posted NSE revenue $376.1M, +74% y/y and above its $360-368M guide, on data-center and aerospace/defense test demand, guided NSE to $426-434M for the December quarter and added a $500M buyback; network/datacenter test demand was still accelerating through Keysight's Aug-Oct quarter.
findings.link: Direct competitor in network/datacenter test: Viavi bought Spirent's high-speed Ethernet/network-security lines ($52.7M in the quarter) while Keysight bought the rest of Spirent; both sell lab and production test to the AI datacenter/transceiver ecosystem, which drives Keysight's Wireline (now larger than Wireless within $1.0bn Commercial Communications).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Keysight's last two prints show demand is not what the stock trades on now; supply conversion is.
findings.why_not_priced: Keysight is lower now (~$286) than on Nov 4 (~$287) after a rebound to ~$305 and back, so the read-across to Keysight orders was not held; if priced, the stock would have kept the Nov 11 level. Sized small because Keysight's limiter is supply, not demand.
findings.independence: Ralliant T&M book-to-bill >1.1 (finding below); Nvidia Q4 guide $130bn (finding below).

findings.finding: Ralliant (Tektronix, reported 2026-11-04) grew Test & Measurement 21% organic with book-to-bill above 1.1, EBITDA margin up to 19.3%, raised full-year guidance, carried $7M of IEEPA tariff refunds, and flagged new 'input inflation and constrained supply'; the stock later traded -12.2%.
findings.link: Tektronix competes with Keysight's oscilloscopes and EISG/general-electronics lab instruments (EISG $501M, 27% of Keysight Q3 revenue); same component supply base.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Peer's beat-and-raise was sold, matching Keysight's own last two prints.
findings.why_not_priced: Offsets: demand positive (b2b >1.1), supply/inflation negative and the reaction negative; net zero. Filed so the judges see a same-season T&M peer selling on a beat with a supply caveat.
findings.independence: Viavi (finding above) same day, demand side; Keysight's own Aug 18 supply remarks.

findings.finding: Nvidia reported on 2026-11-17 revenue $115.8bn (+103% y/y, vs ~$109bn expected) and guided Q4 to $130bn ±3%, confirming the AI-infrastructure build that drives Keysight's Wireline orders (wireline orders more than doubled y/y in Q3) continued through Keysight's quarter and into its Q1.
findings.link: Hyperscalers are ~10% of Keysight sales directly (Truist symposium summary, 2026-09-15) and drive the transceiver, switch and interconnect makers that buy Keysight's 224G analyzers and emulation; Nvidia is the system the ecosystem tests for. Indirect, no revenue share disclosed for Nvidia itself.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Keysight fell over the week containing Nvidia's beat (5-day -6.1%), so the AI-demand read-across has not been paying.
findings.why_not_priced: Macro-to-company transmission, sized small; Keysight's price fell after it, so the market is not crediting AI demand to KEYS, consistent with supply being the binding constraint.
findings.independence: Proxy. Viavi data-center test strength (finding above) points the same way from a direct competitor.

findings.link: Anritsu competes with Keysight in wireless (5G/6G) and datacenter/optical network test; same end markets as Keysight's $1.0bn Commercial Communications.
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly predates Keysight's Aug 18 call, so largely priced; the 'orders ahead of schedule' remark is a pull-forward caution as well as a demand sign. Sized near zero.
